sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; unitary national codification under the Código de Comercio and the Civil Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Andean Community Decision 578 — Common Investment Regime (active)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Decree 410 of 1971 (Código de Comercio, arts. 110-115 and 650); Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT framework); Law 2155 of 2021, art. 91 (creation of the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales — RUB); Decree 1674 of 2021 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (RUB regulation and filing mechanics); Circular 031 of 2013 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (SAGRILAFT); and Decree 1073 of 2015 (fuel distribution regulatory framework).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Existencia y Representación) of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the origin state is a Hague Convention member); otherwise Consular Legalization by the Colombian consulate in the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the legal representative of the future Colombian S.A.S.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed, if required by the Cámara de Comercio, by certification of the signature before a Colombian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of valid passports of all subscribers and natural-person ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or designated public officer in the country of origin of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus Spanish translation by a certified public translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the board of directors or general meeting of each foreign shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Colombian S.A.S., the capital subscription, and the appointment of the local legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or competent corporate body of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the origin state and Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT clearance, good-repute certificate, or criminal-record certificate of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial, police, or dedicated AML registry authority of the UBO's state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening under Law 1121 of 2006, Circular 031 of 2013 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (SAGRILAFT), and UIAF guidance. The pre-incorporation KYC file must screen all shareholders, beneficial owners, directors, and the legal representative against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU terrorist list, UIAF national risk lists, and domestic public records (Procuraduría, Contraloría, judicial criminal records). PEPs are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and continuous monitoring through the corporate lifetime. Screening evidence must be preserved in the AML/CFT file and made available to the Cámara de Comercio, UIAF, and the banking institution for the corporate account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) — www.rues.org.co; name reservation applications are processed by the Cámara de Comercio of the intended registered domicile
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Spanish under Article 111 of the Código de Comercio and Chamber of Commerce practice; foreign-language words or brand elements must be transliterated into the Spanish alphabet before reservation. The S.A.S. name must be a unique denomination followed by the suffix 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada', must not be identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to any existing name in the RUES database, and must not be misleading as to the corporate type, activity, or nationality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Banco', 'Banca', 'Crédito', 'Seguros', 'Aseguradora', 'Capitalización', 'Fondo de Pensiones', 'AFP', 'ARL' — reserved for entities authorized by the Financial Superintendence
'Colombia', 'Nacional', 'República', 'Estado', 'Presidencia', 'Departamento', 'Municipio', 'Gobernación', 'Alcaldía' — require prior authorization of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism
'Cooperativa', 'Fondo de Empleados', 'Asociación Mutual' — reserved for the solidarity economy under supervision of the Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria
'Petróleos', 'Petroquímica', 'Combustibles', 'Gas', 'Hidrocarburos', 'Búnker', 'Marino' — sensitive sector tokens reviewed against the Ministry of Mines and Energy and DIMAR licensing criteria
Reserved legal-type acronyms inconsistent with the S.A.S. form, such as 'S.A.', 'Ltda.', 'E.U.', 'C.A.'
Words contrary to public order, moral standards, or third-party trademarks registered before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 business days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Cámara de Comercio and a subsidiary 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio, in accordance with Law 1437 of 2011 (Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo). The appeal must include a written petition, the Chamber's rejection notice, evidence of distinctiveness (e.g., trademark search), and up to three alternative proposed names. The Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio must decide the appeal within 30 business days; the applicant may also pursue judicial review before the Consejo de Estado if the administrative appeal is denied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office for a licensed offshore marine fuel bunkering entity. The Cámara de Comercio will accept a verifiable municipal address for notification, but the Ministry of Mines and Energy fuel distribution license and the DIMAR / Superintendencia de Puertos y Transportes port authorizations require a physical operational office, fuel-handling capability, and documented commercial substance in the port district of the registered domicile. A shared administrative virtual office may serve only as a transitional notification address during the pre-incorporation and pre-licensing phase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of licensed operations. Joint inspection authority is exercised by the Ministry of Mines and Energy, DIMAR, and the Superintendencia de Puertos y Transportes under Decree 1073 of 2015, with additional surprise audits by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (fuel metering and quality) and DIAN (regulated-fuel tax controls).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and homologation certificate for three proposed corporate names (Certificado de uso de nombre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the intended registered domicile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (derechos de inscripción) published by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of existence and legal representation (Certificado de existencia y representación legal) obtained in the pre-incorporation verification phase
Notarial authentication of the private incorporation document and by-laws (Acta de constitución y estatutos) under Law 1258 of 2008
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public notary (Notaría) of the registered domicile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff scale (tabla de tarifas notariales) of the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile registration of the S.A.S. and payment of the registration fee (matrícula mercantil) in the Registro Único Empresarial
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory progressive tariff on subscribed capital (approximately 0.7% subject to statutory minimum) plus the uniform matrícula mercantil fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office — physical commercial domicile in the selected port jurisdiction (first annual term; e.g., Cartagena, Barranquilla, or Buenaventura)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial domicile service provider or real estate lessor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate registered-address services in the selected port district

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Unified Beneficial Owner Register (RUB) filing — professional preparation and submission support (electronic filing itself is free of charge)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External accountant or tax advisor (public accountant registered before the Junta Central de Contadores)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for RUB compliance preparation under Decree 1674 of 2021 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 2, 4, 5, 17, 22; Código de Comercio, arts. 98–110 (supplementary); Decreto 1074 de 2015, arts. 15–20 (RUES regulations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) – www.rues.org.co; DIAN for tax registration and NIT issuance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Document) or Public Deed when in-kind contributions involve real property; filed in the Registro Mercantil via RUES
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a nominal capital (e.g., COP 1,000,000) is permissible. Shares and capital may be freely agreed by shareholders. No escrow account is mandated by law. If foreign capital is invested, registration with Banco de la República is required within 12 months post-incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the undersigned shareholder of [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. hereby (i) subscribes the entire authorized capital of [NUMBER] shares having no par value, with a total nominal value of [AMOUNT] Colombian pesos, all fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the bylaws; (ii) adopts the corporate bylaws and establishes the registered office at [ADDRESS], municipality, department, Colombia, as the principal place of business; (iii) appoints [REPRESENTATIVE] as sole Legal Representative and [ALTERNATE] as Alternate Legal Representative, with powers to execute documents, open bank accounts, and file before the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN; and (iv) authorizes the payment of all incorporation fees, notarial costs, and registrations, and the taking of all actions necessary to lawfully carry out the corporate purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name through the 'Certificado de Homonimia' request on the RUES platform. The Chamber checks that the name is not identical or unduly similar to an existing registered company. If approved, the name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and up to three alternative names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Filing a fresh name request with alternative names; no separate appeal is available if the name is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (if public deed is required) or private document authenticated by a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the 'Documento Privado de Constitución' containing the full bylaws, share subscription, registered office, and appointment of legal representatives. All shareholders must sign. If any in-kind contribution consists of real estate, a public deed must be executed before a notary; otherwise, the private document must bear notarial acknowledgment of the shareholder's signatures.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if a shareholder is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the document and obtain resignatures; if notarial errors occur, a new deed may be required through a corrective act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office (RUES portal or physical window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document along with the Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial (RUES), the draft Formulario de Registro Único Tributario (RUT), and proof of payment of the registration rights (derechos de inscripción). Upon review, the Chamber registers the company and issues the 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a 'Requerimiento' under Resolution 172 of 2010, correct the stated deficiencies within one month; otherwise, file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' against the rejection on legal merits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – www.dian.gov.co (online) or nearest DIAN branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Formulario RUT through the DIAN online portal or at the DIAN office. After validation, the company receives its provisional NIT and, after the tax account is activated, a definitive NIT. The company should also register as a withholding agent if applicable and request the electronic invoicing signature certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Shareholders' NITs (if local) or foreign tax ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is rejected, verify the commercial registry data with the Chamber and resubmit; or file a correction application (Form 2097) online within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration: bank account opening and legal books legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected financial institution; Secretaría de Hacienda municipal; Cámara de Comercio (for books registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name with the authorized representatives. Register with the municipal tax authorities for Impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA) if business will be conducted in a specific municipality. Also, legalize the corporate books (share register, minutes book, and accounting records) by registering them at the Chamber of Commerce before first use.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Passport or ID of legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Banks may require enhanced due diligence for bunkering activities; complete their KYC/KYB requirements or choose a bank experienced in maritime fuel operations. For ICA, file the required forms or request an exemption if no permanent establishment is present.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Puertos y Transporte (SuperTransporte) coordinated with the Dirección General Marítima (DIMAR) for port and maritime operating permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Servicios Portuarios – Suministro de Combustible a Buques (Bunkering Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA); for coastal ports, the local Corporación Autónoma Regional (e.g., CARDIQUE for Caribbean waters)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Partial EIA (Diagnóstico Ambiental) plus Permiso de Vertimientos and Registro de Emisiones Atmosféricas; full Licencia Ambiental is required if the bunkering operation is integrated into a new port terminal or major infrastructure
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to marine waters: Resolution 631 of 2015 limits – COD ≤ 200 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.0. VOC emissions from fuel transfer: Resolution 909 of 2008 requiere la recuperación de vapores (VOC recovery) y límite de inmisión no mayor a 0.5 mg/m3. Hazardous waste handling under Decree 4741 of 2005; marine fuel product quality per ASTM D2069.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos (local fire department) certification under NFPA 30 and NSR-10 for structural load and fire safety; occupational health and safety (SG-SST) clearance under Resolution 0312 of 2019, including risk assessment and emergency response protocols, submitted to the ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN - Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (National Tax and Customs Authority). Principal electronic portals: MUISCA (Modelo Unico de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) for registration, filing, and payments; and the SIE (Sistema Informatico Electronico) for mandatory real-time electronic invoice clearance. Official website: www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned or foreign-managed S.A.S. obtains its NIT (Numero de Identificacion Tributaria) as follows: (i) execute the public incorporation deed before the Camara de Comercio of the registered seat and register the entity in the RUES (Registro Unico Empresarial y Social); (ii) appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia (or a resident tax agent ('apoderado') with express general powers when the S.A.S. is administered from abroad); (iii) complete the RUT (Registro Unico Tributario) pre-registration in MUISCA, selecting the activity codes for ISIC 5222 ancillary water-transport support, the 'responsable del regimen comun' VAT status, exporter status, and the marine fuel supply flag; (iv) obtain the digital PKI certificate for the legal representative; (v) await DIAN validation and issuance of the definitive 9-to-12 digit NIT with check digit, which activates the electronic invoicing account. Processing time is 2-5 business days. The company must also register in the SICEX/VUCE exporter registry and, where the bunkering activity involves customs-bonded fuel storage, complete the applicable DIAN and maritime authority authorizations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Colombian S.A.S. is a separate, full taxpayer under the ordinary regime. It pays corporate income tax (CIT) on worldwide income at the 35% statutory rate for fiscal years 2023-2025, municipal ICA tax on industrial and commercial activities (generally 0.2%-1.4% of gross revenues), and VAT as a common-regime responsible taxpayer. The S.A.S. cannot be treated as a pass-through or disregarded entity and no US-style check-the-box classification is recognized. Profits distributed to non-resident shareholders are generally subject to a 10% dividend withholding tax once the entity-level CIT has been settled. Non-resident shareholders are not liable for entity-level taxes, but Colombia's CFC rules apply to certain passive income of foreign-controlled entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; entity classification is statutory. Available elections: (i) the SIMPLE regime (Ley 1943/2018, as reformed by Ley 2277/2022), an optional single presumptive national tax available to entities with gross income of not more than 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,980 million for 2025) meeting the statutory conditions, replacing ordinary CIT and ICA; (ii) the Article 481(c) E.T. exemption flag for bunker fuel and lubricants supplied to international-traffic vessels; (iii) advance pricing agreements (APA) with DIAN on transfer-pricing matters; (iv) customs regime elections, including Zona Franca status for deferred VAT and customs duty on stored marine fuels; (v) the election to channel export proceeds through the official foreign-exchange market and to request the Banco de la Republica extension of the 6-month collection deadline under Circular DCIN-83. Deductions of payments structured to exploit hybrid entities or hybrid financial instruments are restricted by Colombia's anti-hybrid rules enacted under Law 2277/2022 (BEPS Action 2).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Comité de Régimen de Cambios in issuing the foreign exchange statute, and with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) in enforcing customs and cross-border currency controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is fully convertible in practice for current-account transactions, including trade and ordinary services; foreign investment and profit remittances are permitted for registered capital inflows under the regime of Inversión Internacional de Capital. Bunkering services are classified as an export of services for exchange-register purposes, and the Colombian operator may invoice in USD. Capital-account transactions, including domestic borrowing in foreign currency, external credit and FDI liquidation, require declarations and registration with Banco de la República through a permitted foreign-exchange intermediary. Profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is subject to corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax, plus compliance with the annual exchange declaration; profits may be remitted once the audited financial statements measure taxable distributable profits and the investment is registered in Banco de la República's investment balance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a mandatory conversion ratio or forced surrender of export currency receipts. The operative requirement is channeling through the authorized exchange market: export proceeds from bunkering and marine refueling services must be received into Colombia through an authorized intermediary (commercial bank, financial corporation or exchange house) within the statutory term established by Banco de la República from the date of invoice or export registration. Exporters may keep the foreign currency in a local foreign-currency account or convert it into COP at the market exchange rate, but the proceeds must enter the local financial system by the deadline and the related Declaración de Cambio must be filed. The precise calendar term fluctuates with prevailing regulation and should be verified against Banco de la República Resolution 3/2020 and its updated annexes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for fully digital non-bank EMIs. Colombian law does not recognize a separate EMI license that allows foreign digital banks to open domestic settlement accounts or clear Colombian pesos on their own balance sheet. Cross-border fintechs may be engaged only as payment facilitators acting through a licensed Colombian bank; the bank remains the paying account keeper. For a marine bunkering scope rated Medium_Risk_Enhanced, local tier-1 banks require a physical or insured banking counterparty, and fintech-led onboarding with no local regulated custodian is generally rejected by Colombian compliance officers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Colombian tier-1 banks require at least one legal representative or controlling shareholder of the S.A.S. to appear physically at the bank's compliance branch for an enhanced onboarding interview. Remote opening is formally tolerated through video identification and a notarized power of attorney, but for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced marine bunkering entity, an in-person interview at the corporate banking office in Bogotá, Cartagena or Barranquilla is normally mandatory; all corporate documents, passports and UBO declarations must be notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate shell without physical operating premises in Colombia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cámara de Comercio certificate of incorporation and current legal representation; lease agreements for port-side offices, storage or fuel depot terminals; payroll records and social security filings showing local staff; business continuity and insurance policies; photos/video of storage, equipment, and bunkering site.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership behind the Colombian S.A.S.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized UBO declarations identifying all natural persons with direct or indirect control or ownership of 5% or more; DIAN tax residency certificates; audited consolidated financial statements of the parent group; bank reference letters from recognized foreign correspondent banks; sworn affidavit explaining source of funds for capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or suspicious vessel flag, bareboat charter or customer country risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screened OFAC/EU/United Nations sanctions lists on all vessel owners, operators, charters and customers; independent maritime security vetting report; AIS/vessel-tracking records during operations; contractual requirement to pay each voyage in named bank accounts; flag and port-of-call compliance matrix; designated as a bunker supplier by local maritime authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient transactional documentation for marine fuel delivery and possible financing of fuel smuggling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated bunker delivery fuel receipts stating vessel IMO number, fuel type, ISO 8217 grade, quantity, delivery port and supplier stamps; sale invoices matching customs and DIAN records; weight or volumetric certificates; port authority notifications; commercial invoices and Standby LC or SWIFT MT103 references; payable/guarantee resolutions of the S.A.S.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound foreign direct investment capital injection is received by the S.A.S. only through a Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary. The foreign parent sends a SWIFT MT103 wire to the bank account of the S.A.S., issuing the wire with purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment and the beneficiary's NIT. The bank must present a 'Declaración de Cambio' to Banco de la República evidencing the inflow, and the S.A.S. must register the investment under the national FDI registration system. The required documentation includes a certification of incorporation, share ownership registry, UBO declaration, banking account number, and board resolution approving the capital injection; the bank will verify that the name of the foreign transferor matches the registered parent and will reject third-party unconnected transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary outbound clearing rail for bunker procurement and marine supplies is SWIFT MT103 for direct transfers to foreign suppliers, with MT202 optional for bank-to-bank transfers. For larger fuel contracts, the S.A.S. will issue a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 with the bank acting as issuing bank; a Standby LC under ISP98 may support performance obligations when the Colombian buyer or counterparty supplies partial fuel into a vessel. Domestic COP disbursements are cleared through the Colombian CUD (Cámara de Riesgo Central de Colombia) ACH system, while USD disbursements use correspondent banking via the United States or European clearing institutions. All outgoing payments require a exchange declaration, underlying invoice and, for foreign debt payments, prior Banco de la República registration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC USD-COP forward contracts entered into with an authorized local commercial bank, backed by real underlying fuel or service receivables/payables.
USD-COP currency swaps executed with a Colombian bank for matching FX exposure on triangular bunkering contracts.

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) referencing COP entered into offshore solely for non-resident counterparties or central clearers outside Colombia; Colombian resident entities are required to route forward contracts through local banks and can only settle a net difference in COP.
FX options and Range Forwards for hedging declared trade invoices and procurement quotas, subject to Banco de la República suitability rules.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for capital-grade foreign debt and financing of port storage assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Local Chamber of Commerce operating the Single Business Registry – RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March, fixed calendar-year statutory deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Moratory interest on the unpaid renewal tariff; administrative fine of up to 3 SMMLV (approx. USD 975) under Code of Commerce Art. 12; failure to renew for five consecutive years triggers administrative cancellation (strike-off) of the merchant registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementario (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the DIAN filing window from mid-February to late April of the following fiscal year; exact date assigned by the last two digits of the NIT in the DIAN tax calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneity fine of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax, with a minimum fine of approx. USD 200; monthly late-payment interest of 1.5%; criminal liability for omission under Tax Penal Code Art. 434.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Informe de Beneficiario Final (Annual UBO Confirmation Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter (mid-January to mid-March); exact date determined by the last digit of the NIT under DIAN Resolution 164/2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of COP 1,000,000 (approx. USD 250) per month of delay, capped under Tax Code Art. 651 at 1% of gross income or COP 20,000,000 (approx. USD 5,000) where no gross income; legal representative and revisor fiscal jointly liable; DIAN compliance certificates blocked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Estados Financieros con Dictamen (Audited Financial Statements Filed with Supervisory Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades (submitted via SII – Sistema de Información Integral)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the July–September window after the fiscal year-end; date assigned by the last digit of the NIT in the Supersociedades SII calendar (FY2023: 9 July – 27 September 2024)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Institutional fine of up to 200 SMMLV (approx. USD 65,000) and personal fine on the legal representative of up to 50 SMMLV (approx. USD 16,250); non-filing blocks the certificate of compliance and can trigger regulatory intervention.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación del Permiso de Suministro de Combustible Marino (Marine Bunkering Permit Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIMAR (Dirección General Marítima) and the Port Captaincy (Capitanía de Puerto) of the operation port
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary date of permit issuance; renewal application must be filed at least 30 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expired permit automatically suspends all bunkering operations; administrative fine under the DIMAR maritime tariff schedule (approx. USD 250 – 25,000 by severity); aggravated operation without a permit exposes the vessel to seizure and revocation of the fuel-supply authorization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) when prior-year gross assets exceed COP 6,500 million (5,000 SMMLV, approx. USD 1.6 million) or gross revenue exceeds COP 3,900 million (3,000 SMMLV, approx. USD 975,000); an ISIC 5222 marine bunkering and refueling operation normally exceeds the revenue threshold and additionally requires statutory audit under the maritime commerce regulations applicable to licensed fuel-supply activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian accounting framework under Law 1314/2009: full IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF Plenas, Grupo 1) for entities exceeding 30,000 SMMLV in assets or with public-interest status; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes, Grupo 2) for all other SAS entities; supervising authority is the CTCP for interpretation and Supersociedades for enforcement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative and the revisor fiscal jointly file the annual UBO confirmation with DIAN each year in the first quarter; any transfer of shares or change in ownership of a holder of 5% or more (voting rights or economic benefit) must be updated in the DIAN UBO system within 15 days of the transfer registration and recorded in the beneficiaries book; the annual filing restates the full chain of control through direct shareholders, indirect natural persons, trusts, and offshore vessel-owning structures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Final Beneficiaries (Libro de Beneficiario Final)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea y Junta Directiva)
Share Transfer Ledger (Libro de Registro de Transferencias de Acciones)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to 900 per year for a Chamber-of-Commerce-registered domicile address and virtual office agent in Bogotá, Cartagena, or Barranquilla
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 to 9,000 per year for a qualified revisor fiscal covering monthly statutory visits and the annual audited financial statements of an ISIC 5222 bunkering operation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Colombia imposes a 35% corporate income tax (CIT) rate for taxable year 2024 and onwards. Certain strategic port infrastructure and maritime logistics investments may qualify for the deduction of up to 25% of qualifying fixed asset investments (Ley 1819 de 2016, Article 158-3) and the benefit of free trade zone (Zona Franca) regimes reducing CIT to 20% for predominantly export-oriented or port-related operators where applicable. The so-called 'dry' services for international maritime traffic by non-resident-owned Colombian entities may trigger presumption rules; specific sectoral incentives are limited absent actual infrastructure investment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) via DIAN electronic portal (Muisca)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed and paid within the deadline established by DIAN Resolution each year, typically between the 8th and 23rd business days of April for entities whose taxable year-end is December 31. Entities with a different statutory year-end must file within three (3) months thereof; extensions are not generally available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross taxable income from all activities, including bunkering sales, marine fuel supply commissions, and ancillary lubricant replenishment revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned S.A.S. entity reports global Colombian-source income only; foreign-source income attributable to a permanent establishment in Colombia must be included. Bunkering revenues derived from international voyages to Colombian ports are taxed under Colombian source rules; income from operations outside Colombia is not taxable unless effectively connected to the Colombian branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, including income expressly excluded by the Colombian Tax Code (e.g., certain export incentives, income of foreign shipping enterprises under Article 124 when reciprocal treatment applies).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned S.A.S. should claim only the exclusions legally available to Colombian domestic entities. The Article 124 exemption for foreign shipping companies generally does not apply to a Colombian S.A.S.; instead, income from international maritime operations may be subject to the normal 35% rate unless a tax treaty or special bunkering regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and deductions attributable to generating taxable income, including procurement of marine fuels, vessel logistical support, port agent fees, crew replenishment supplies, depreciation of storage and bunker barge assets, and financing interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only if they are necessary, proportional, and supported by invoices and bank payment trails. Transfer pricing rules require that cross-border purchases of fuel or lubricants from related parties be priced at arm's length; otherwise, the deduction may be disallowed, recharacterized, or penalized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before current-year loss compensation and tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the aggregate result after applying prior-year loss carryforwards (limited to 5 taxable years) and any free trade zone or port infrastructure investment deductions. Non-resident investors may not allocate head-office general expenses to the Colombian S.A.S. unless a valid TP policy exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments. This is the base upon which the 35% rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that all transfer pricing adjustments and thin capitalization limits have been considered. Interest paid to related non-resident lenders exceeding the 30% EBITDA limitation (or the applicable ratio) must be added back.
Final tax due after applying tax credits, withholding tax credits (including the 7.5% or 10% remittance tax credit where applicable), and any self-withholding certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax due. A minimum penalty of 10 UVT applies when there is no tax due. Late payment interest accrues at the current effective bank lending rate (tasa de interés moratorio), revised periodically by DIAN. Inaccuracies may attract a penalty equal to 100% of the greater of the understated tax or 10% of the omitted value, and under anti-abuse rules could be increased to 300%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends paid to non-resident individuals or foreign legal entities from profits generated after 2017 that have already been subject to the 35% CIT; dividends paid to Colombian resident entities are not subject to withholding at the corporate level when distributed from taxed profits. A 35% withholding tax (plus an additional 10% on the post-remittance balance) applies to excessive or preferential dividend distributions not supported by audited retained earnings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia's DTA network includes treaties with Canada, Chile, India, Israel, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Portugal, Spain, the United Kingdom, and several other jurisdictions. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction within the applicable calendar year; (ii) provide the Colombian entity with the certificate before the dividend payment or withholding event; and (iii) file the corresponding information return (Form 2276) with the DIAN. The Colombian payer must retain a copy for five (5) years and validate that the recipient is the beneficial owner. Reduced rates depend on the specific treaty; e.g., Spain and the UK generally limit dividend withholding to 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the capital. If the protocol is not timely completed, the statutory 10% rate applies and a subsequent refund may be pursued via a formal DIAN reimbursement procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: interest paid to non-residents is generally subject to a 15% withholding tax; royalties for IP and technical services to a 33.33% withholding tax (or 15% for certain technological services). Treaty rates may reduce interest withholding to 5-10% and royalties to 10% (e.g., Spain, Chile), but only where the beneficial owner and the applicable limitation-on-benefits clause are satisfied. For bunkering entities financing vessel acquisitions or floating inventory through related-party debt, thin-capitalization rules disallow interest deductions exceeding the 30% EBITDA ratio.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual gross income exceeding COP 100,000 million (approx. USD 25 million depending on FX) triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; separate thresholds apply for taxpayers with total gross income exceeding COP 10,000 million or net worth exceeding COP 50,000 million regarding country-by-country reporting obligations. Even below the documentation threshold, every Colombian S.A.S. must apply arm's length principles to cross-border related-party transactions and complete the set of TP disclosure annexes (Form 2448/Measuring Forms).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are formally embedded in the transfer pricing and anti-avoidance framework (Ley 1819, Articles 260-1 to 260-11 and OECD-aligned 2023 revisions). A Colombian S.A.S. engaged in bunkering must demonstrate that its decision-making, operational management, and risk-taking activities occur in Colombia. Existence of physical staff, fuel procurement contracts, port agency agreements, vessel scheduling logs, and significant accounting records is mandatory. The shell-company doctrine permits DIAN to disregard legal form, recharacterize transactions, impose a 35% tax on artificial profits, and apply gross-up penalties where the entity lacks operational substance. Marine bunkering additionally requires a valid maritime fuel supplier license (Dirección General Marítima - DIMAR) and compliance with environmental and customs regimes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: deliberately understating bunkering fuel sales, issuing false invoices, disguising related-party commissions, or misrepresenting the vessel destination to avoid Colombian-source classification, thereby defeating the collection of taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 4 to 9 years (Article 434 of the Colombian Criminal Code), fines of 200% of the evaded tax amount, and mandatory forfeiture of assets used in the commission of the offense. DIAN may additionally disregard transactions, impose a 200% accuracy penalty, and deny deductions. Directors and officers of the S.A.S. face an additional civil penalty equal to one (1) to five (5) times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is expressly permitted under Article 42 of Law 1258 of 2008 for tax fraud and abuse of the S.A.S. form. Directors who signed false returns may be joint and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, face travel bans under the DIAN administrative enforcement (restricción de salida del país), and be subject to extradition where a bilateral or multilateral criminal assistance treaty exists.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Colombian S.A.S. for tax residence benefits without real operational substance, e.g., no employees, no physical fuel storage capacity, no procurement or vessel scheduling functions, and all contracts concluded remotely by foreign beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may recharacterize the entire arrangement, treat the foreign parent as possessing a Colombian permanent establishment, impose the 35% CIT plus sanctions, and disallow transfer pricing adjustments. The reputational and administrative penalties include a tax penalty of 20% of the omitted taxable base or the value of the improper benefit, and potential closure of the establishment by Customs (DIAN) for operating without a valid license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allowed the S.A.S. to fail economic substance requirements are jointly liable for the assessed taxes and penalties. Under Article 43 of Law 1258, judicial authorities may impose prohibitions on contracting with the State and deregister the entity. Travel bans and freezing of personal bank accounts of foreign signatories have been enforced in recent DIAN proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Cash & Fuel Smuggling Financial Movement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving bunkering payments via unidentified crypto-assets, bearer structured cash deposits, or intra-group prepayments from shell jurisdictions without the required AML customer due diligence, or invoicing to embargoed vessels or individuals on Colombian OFAC-linked lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Colombian Law 1121 of 2006 and Amended Criminal Code, money laundering carries a penalty of 9 to 15 years imprisonment and a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 minimum monthly wages. UIAF (Financial Intelligence Unit) may impose administrative fines on the S.A.S. for failure to adopt the SARLAFT (anti-money laundering accountability) system. Vigilant enforcement under Resolution 2021-00580 of the Superintendence of Companies allows fines up to COP 800 million per infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML breaches when they intentionally or negligently bypass protocols. The corporate veil may be pierced, personal assets seized, and the director prohibited from travelling abroad. Criminal exposure extends to imprisonment for tax fraud and conspiracy to smuggle fuel, with no corporate indemnification available.
